s.description: Two large reindeer herding cooperatives must choose routes for moving their herds during the same seasonal migration. Cooperative A chooses between Mountain Pass and River Valley, while Cooperative B chooses between Coastal Track and Forest Corridor.

s.name: Eel Pass Inspections
s.description: A river authority is choosing how to inspect an eel pass before a high-stakes operating period. The hydropower operator is choosing whether to open the gates or restrict flow during that period.

s.name: Seasonal Salt Pans
s.description: Two neighboring salt-pan operators are planning their harvest for the coming season. The first operator chooses between Early drawdown and Staged drawdown, while the second chooses between Shared channels and Separate channels for moving brine through the pans.

s.name: Winter Hive Siting
s.description: Two neighboring beekeepers are deciding where to site their small apiaries for winter. Beekeeper A chooses between Windbreak Side and Sunny Side, while Beekeeper B chooses between Creek Edge and Orchard Edge.

s.name: Orchard Falconry Visit
s.description: A falconer and a nearby orchard grower coordinate a routine visit to discourage pests. The falconer chooses between Perch Patrol and Field Patrol, while the grower chooses between Morning Access and Afternoon Access.

s.name: Planetarium Scheduling
s.description: A small planetarium coordinator chooses whether to place a new show in an early or late slot. A guest-program curator chooses whether to align the program with that slot or keep the program in its usual format.

s.name: Kiln Schedule
s.description: Two major charcoal producers, North Ridge Charcoal and Ember Valley Charcoal, must schedule a high-volume kiln run. Each chooses either Night Burn or Day Burn while using the same regional woodstock and kiln capacity.

s.name: Cranberry Bog Flooding
s.description: A cranberry grower is deciding whether to open the bog's floodgates or hold the water in place. A neighboring grower upstream is choosing whether to release water toward the shared drainage channel or retain it on their side.

s.name: Orchard Falconry Contract
s.description: A regional orchard cooperative and a licensed falconer are planning a season-long pest-control contract. The cooperative chooses between Early Release and Late Release for when hawks begin work, while the falconer chooses between Broad Patrol and Targeted Patrol for how to cover the orchards.

s.name: Seaweed Rack Spacing
s.description: Two neighboring seaweed growers are adjusting their small drying racks for the day. Grower A chooses between Close Slats and Open Slats, while Grower B chooses between a Raised Rack and a Ground Rack.

s.name: Kelp Harvest Schedule
s.description: A small kelp farmer is choosing between a steady harvest and a bulk harvest. A nearby kelp buyer is choosing between morning pickup and afternoon pickup.

s.name: Mountain Hut Resupply
s.description: A mountain hut manager chooses between “Full Load” and “Lean Load” for the season’s resupply plan. A helicopter operator chooses between “Early Flight” and “Late Flight” for the delivery schedule.

s.name: Herbarium Loan Scheduling
s.description: A regional herbarium curator and a university botanist are arranging a loan of preserved plant specimens. The curator chooses between Standard Terms and Flexible Terms, while the botanist chooses between a Short Loan and an Extended Loan.

s.name: Weir Maintenance Window
s.description: A ditch keeper and a small downstream farm manager are coordinating a routine weir maintenance window. The ditch keeper chooses Early closure or Late closure, and the farm manager chooses Shift watering or Keep schedule.

s.name: Marathon Road Closures
s.description: For a city marathon, the race director and the transit authority jointly plan road access for race day. The race director chooses between Full Closure and Rolling Closure, while the transit authority chooses between Early Reroute and Late Reroute. Their choices set the operating plan for a season-significant race and transit budget.

s.name: Stone Wall Repair Bid
s.description: A homeowner and a local mason are arranging a small stone wall repair bid. The homeowner chooses between a Detailed Scope and a Quick Scope, while the mason chooses between a Firm Bid and a Flexible Bid.

s.name: Garden Hedge Contract
s.description: A homeowner and a local hedge-laying contractor are arranging a modest garden-boundary contract. The homeowner chooses either Firm scope, which specifies the hedge’s length and finish in advance, or Flexible scope, which leaves those details open; the contractor chooses either Full quote, with a detailed written estimate, or Quick quote, with a brief estimate.

s.name: Planetarium Premiere
s.description: A national planetarium network and a private space agency are each scheduling a high-stakes premiere about a newly discovered exoplanet. The network chooses between the Prime slot and the Late slot, while the agency chooses between the Prime slot and the Late slot.

s.name: Small-Batch Vinyl Queue
s.description: A small record label and a local pressing plant are coordinating one modest vinyl pressing queue. The label chooses between Standard run and Fine-tune run, while the plant chooses between Keep slot and Shift slot.

s.name: Clocktower Festival Season
s.description: A municipal clock conservator chooses between a Full Overhaul and Targeted Repair for the town clocktower before the festival season. The festival director chooses between Public Chimes and Quiet Hours for the tower's operating schedule.

s.name: Salt Pan Timing
s.description: Two neighboring salt-pan harvesters are making a small timing choice for an ordinary day's crystal collection. Each chooses either Morning Rake, beginning the fine adjustment early, or Afternoon Rake, leaving it until later.

s.name: Dye-House Scheduling
s.description: Two textile manufacturers with major export orders must schedule their dyeing runs at a shared industrial dye house. Mill A chooses Early shift or Late shift, and Mill B chooses Early shift or Late shift.

s.name: Millpond Sluice Timing
s.description: An upstream millkeeper and a downstream millkeeper are coordinating use of the same millpond. Each chooses whether to open their sluice early or late during the day's milling.

s.name: Seasonal Hedge Contract
s.description: An estate manager and a hedge-laying contractor are setting terms for a substantial season-long hedge restoration contract. The manager chooses between Early laying and Late laying, while the contractor chooses between a Fixed crew and a Flexible crew.

s.name: Wind-Farm Maintenance Window
s.description: A wind-farm operator is planning maintenance for a major generating site and chooses between Routine Overhaul and Targeted Repair. A regional grid coordinator chooses between Early Outage and Deferred Outage for the maintenance window.

s.name: Woodland Truffle Permits
s.description: Two neighboring hobby foragers, A and B, are applying for permits for visits to a small woodland patch. Each chooses between a Dawn Slot and a Dusk Slot for routine truffle foraging.

s.name: Stadium Snack Pricing
s.description: A stadium concessionaire and a nearby concession partner are setting their menu strategies for a game day. Each chooses between a Premium Menu and a Value Menu for the stadium crowd.

s.name: Port Dredging Windows
s.description: A port authority and a shipping consortium are planning a substantial channel-dredging season. The port authority chooses between Early Window and Late Window, while the consortium chooses between Shift Schedule and Keep Schedule for its vessel program.

s.name: Flour Contract
s.description: A regional flour mill and a national bakery group are coordinating a high-stakes flour order for a major contract. The mill chooses between Rush Shipment and Standard Shipment, while the bakery group chooses between Reserve Stock and Spot Buy.

s.name: Herbarium Loan Requests
s.description: A university herbarium curator and a visiting botanist are arranging a modest specimen loan. The curator chooses either Rapid Review or Full Review, while the botanist chooses either Standard Request or Detailed Request.

s.name: Routine Rail Handoff
s.description: A small freight-rail operator chooses Early Slot or Late Slot for a routine interchange. A neighboring short-line dispatcher chooses Steady Pace or Quick Pace for handling that same handoff.

s.name: Seasonal Kiln Booking
s.description: Two independent ceramic studios are booking firings in a shared regional kiln for high-profile seasonal collections. Studio A chooses between Fast firing and Slow firing, while Studio B chooses between Early firing and Late firing.

s.name: Evening Planetarium Slots
s.description: A neighborhood planetarium and a school planetarium are arranging shows on the same modest evening calendar. Each chooses either First Slot or Second Slot for its regular presentation.

s.name: Heritage Thatching Season
s.description: A national thatching cooperative and a heritage-estate consortium must coordinate a major season of roof restoration. The cooperative chooses between “Early Rota” and “Late Rota,” while the consortium chooses between “Full Access” and “Restricted Access” for the thatching sites.

s.name: Shared Vineyard Canal
s.description: Two neighboring vineyard growers share a small irrigation canal during a routine watering day. Grower A chooses between Early watering and Late watering, while Grower B chooses between Morning release and Afternoon release.

s.name: The Landmark Edition
s.description: A major publisher and a letterpress workshop are preparing a high-stakes edition whose production choice could materially affect both parties. The publisher chooses between Early Press and Late Press, while the workshop chooses between Fresh Type and Stored Type.

s.name: Turbine Service Planning
s.description: A wind-farm operator and a maintenance contractor are coordinating a routine service visit for a turbine. The operator chooses between “Schedule service” and “Postpone service,” while the contractor chooses between “Full crew” and “Lean crew.”

s.name: Cable Ferry Timing
s.description: A small cable ferry is making routine crossings on a quiet channel. The ferry operator chooses between “Steady pull” and “Gentle pull,” while the landing assistant chooses between “Early signal” and “Late signal” as a fine adjustment to coordinating the line.

s.name: Wool Scouring Capacity
s.description: A regional wool cooperative and a wool-scouring mill are coordinating a season's processing capacity. The cooperative chooses either Consolidated Lots or Split Lots: larger scheduled batches or smaller batches of fleece. The mill chooses either Reserved Slots or Spot Slots for handling the wool.

s.name: Vineyard Irrigation
s.description: Two neighboring vineyard growers are making a fine irrigation adjustment for a small shared block of vines. The first grower chooses between Early pulse and Late pulse, while the second chooses between Steady flow and Split flow.

s.name: Mushroom Substrate Supply
s.description: A neighborhood mushroom grower and a local substrate supplier are arranging a routine week's substrate supply. The grower chooses between Early Order and Flexible Order, while the supplier chooses between Reserve Batch and Spot Batch.

s.name: Island Ferry Slots
s.description: A regional ferry operator and a port authority are setting the season's timetable for a heavily used island route. The operator chooses between Early Sailing and Late Sailing for its key ferry, while the port authority chooses between Morning Slot and Evening Slot for a connecting ferry service.

s.name: Freight Corridor Timetable
s.description: A national freight railroad and a major port authority are coordinating a high-stakes cargo corridor. The railroad chooses between “Add locomotives” and “Hold capacity,” while the port authority chooses between “Priority slots” and “Shared slots” for the timetable.

s.name: Small Vinyl Run
s.description: A small record label chooses whether to send its lacquer master as an Early master or a Revised master for one modest release. A neighborhood pressing plant chooses between a Short queue and a Full queue for fitting that release into its vinyl pressing schedule.

s.name: Bat Survey Nights
s.description: A volunteer bat-monitoring team chooses between a Quiet Survey, using a low-noise route, and a Broad Survey, covering more observation stations. A park coordinator chooses between Open Access for the survey team and Timed Access with an arranged entry window.

s.name: Canal Lock Scheduling
s.description: A regional canal authority and a freight cooperative are setting a lock schedule for the coming shipping season, with substantial implications for deliveries, operating costs, and the authority’s reputation. The authority chooses either Staggered Windows or Batch Convoys, while the cooperative chooses either Early Slots or Late Slots.

s.name: Global Coffee Sourcing
s.description: A multinational coffee roastery and a major coffee-growing cooperative are making high-stakes sourcing decisions for their flagship supply agreement. Each must choose between Long Contract, which commits them to a fixed relationship, and Spot Market, which leaves the purchase to current-market transactions.

s.name: Seasonal Dune Fences
s.description: A coastal municipality is deciding whether to place its seasonal dune fence along the landward edge or closer to the beach. A nearby resort operator is choosing whether to place its own fence along the boardwalk line or shift it toward the main access path.

s.name: Glacier Survey Flights
s.description: Two polar research agencies are coordinating a high-stakes glacier survey flight campaign whose results will shape major ice and water planning decisions. Agency A chooses between Full Traverse and Perimeter Pass, while Agency B chooses between Shared Corridor and Separate Corridor for the flights.

s.name: Shared Focus Window
s.description: Two observing teams share one small observatory dome session. Team A chooses when to make a fine focus adjustment—Early adjustment or Late adjustment—and Team B makes the same choice for its own telescope setup.

s.name: Textile Dyeing Shifts
s.description: A small textile mill's dyeing supervisor chooses an Early Shift or Late Shift for the dye crew. The finishing coordinator independently chooses an Early Shift or Late Shift for the related finishing work.

s.name: Urban Hive Siting
s.description: A commercial beekeeper and a city planning office are coordinating an urban hive placement for the coming season. The beekeeper chooses between Rooftop Hives and Courtyard Hives, while the planning office chooses between Park Buffer and Street Buffer.

s.name: Small Archive Scanning
s.description: A local archivist and a digitisation technician are preparing a small batch of fragile records. The archivist chooses between Gentle Scan and Sharper Scan, while the technician chooses between Quick Check and Full Check for the same batch.

s.name: Kiln Firing Contract
s.description: A high-volume ceramics manufacturer chooses between Rapid firing and Staged firing for a structural-tile batch. Its kiln-fuel supplier chooses between Reserved fuel and Flexible fuel for the same firing window, with the project important to both businesses.

s.name: Port Dredging Windows
s.description: A port authority is scheduling a routine channel-dredging job and chooses either an Early window or a Late window. A dredging contractor chooses either a Standard crew or a Flexible crew for the work plan.

s.name: Migration Station Slots
s.description: A national bird-monitoring agency and a conservation consortium are negotiating access to scarce bird-ringing station slots during a migration season with major consequences for a population assessment. The agency chooses between Peak Allocation and Reserve Allocation, while the consortium chooses between Dawn Campaign and Dusk Campaign for deploying its ringing teams.

s.name: Yard Timing
s.description: A local freight dispatcher chooses between an Early Slot and a Late Slot for a routine train handoff. A neighboring yard coordinator chooses between a Short Hold and a Long Hold while arranging that same handoff.

s.name: Glacier Survey Flights
s.description: A glacier research agency must choose between flying Repeat Transects over previously mapped ice or surveying New Transects for the season's mapping program. An aerial survey contractor must choose between an Early Launch and a Late Launch while coordinating the flights, with the campaign affecting its seasonal budget and professional reputation.

s.name: Cranberry Bog Flooding
s.description: An upstream cranberry grower and a downstream cranberry grower are managing connected bogs during a severe flood threat. Each chooses between “Open Spillway” and “Hold Water” as their flood-management plan.

s.name: Saffron Picking Plan
s.description: A small saffron grower and a seasonal picking coordinator are arranging one ordinary harvest day's labour. The grower chooses between Fine Tune, adjusting assignments around the flower beds, and Standard Pace, keeping the usual routine; the coordinator chooses between Steady Crew, keeping pickers together, and Flexible Crew, shifting them between beds as needed.

s.name: Bird-Ringing Station Slots
s.description: A bird-ringing station is scheduling a station team and a visiting bird group for the day. The station team chooses Morning Slot or Afternoon Slot, and the visiting group makes the same choice.

s.name: Seasonal Thatching Rotas
s.description: A lead thatching crew and a regional roofing cooperative are coordinating a season of high-profile heritage-roof work. The lead crew chooses Early Rota, keeping its team on the roofs from spring, or Split Rota, alternating crews across the season; the cooperative chooses Fixed Handoff, changing crews on a planned date, or Flexible Handoff, adjusting that date during the season.

s.name: Cider Press Bookings
s.description: Two large cider producers, Orchard North and Orchard South, are arranging access to a scarce regional cider press before harvest. Orchard North chooses between Early booking and Late booking, while Orchard South chooses between Early booking and Late booking.

s.name: Satellite Downlink Windows
s.description: A small satellite operator chooses between requesting an early downlink window or a late downlink window. A partner ground-station scheduler chooses between reserving a slot or sharing a slot for the transmission.

s.name: Dome Time Allocation
s.description: A university observatory team and a visiting consortium must coordinate use of the same telescope dome during a heavily contested observing season. The university team chooses between Deep Survey, which schedules extended coverage of a target field, and Rapid Follow-up, which reserves time for prompt observations; the consortium chooses between Long Exposure, which holds the dome for lengthy integrations, and Short Exposure, which uses briefer observing blocks.

s.name: Ferry Timetable Slots
s.description: Two small ferry operators are arranging departures on the same short route. Each operator chooses either an Earlier slot or a Later slot for its sailing.

s.name: Puppet Tour Stop
s.description: A small puppet theatre troupe is arranging a touring stop with a neighborhood arts center. The troupe chooses between Compact Set and Full Set, while the arts center chooses between Matinee Show and Evening Show.

s.name: Seasonal Ale Distribution
s.description: A regional microbrewery is deciding whether to sell its seasonal ale mainly through a taproom launch or through a distributor push. Its distribution partner is choosing between priority placement for the ale across retail accounts and standard placement.

s.name: Greenhouse Heat Sharing
s.description: During a severe cold snap, two neighboring commercial greenhouses must coordinate how to use a shared heating loop. Greenhouse A chooses between “Open Valve” and “Hold Heat,” while Greenhouse B chooses between “Share Heat” and “Reserve Heat” for its own facility.

s.name: Oyster Bed Lease Renewal
s.description: Two neighboring oyster growers are renewing leases for adjoining beds. Grower A chooses between a Compact Lease and a Broad Lease, while Grower B chooses between Shared Access and Separate Access.

s.name: Orchard Harvest Contract
s.description: An orchard cooperative and a juice company are negotiating a harvest contract. The cooperative chooses between Early Pickup, scheduling the contracted fruit for an earlier collection window, and Late Pickup, scheduling it later; the juice company chooses between Firm Price, setting the purchase price in advance, and Flexible Price, allowing the price terms to adjust during the contract.

s.name: The Archive Acquisition
s.description: A national library and a university library are independently pursuing the exclusive acquisition of a renowned private archive, a deal large enough to reshape their collections and budgets. The national library chooses Public Bid or Quiet Offer, while the university library chooses Public Bid or Quiet Offer.

s.name: Stadium Snack Pricing
s.description: The stadium's main concession operator is choosing between Regular Prices and Combo Deals for an upcoming game. A nearby independent vendor is choosing between Regular Prices and Value Prices for its own stand.

s.name: Small Book Order
s.description: A small public library is fine-tuning a modest order of new local-interest books with an independent distributor. The librarian chooses whether to send a Broad List or a Tight List of titles, while the distributor chooses whether to give a Quick Quote or a Detailed Quote.

s.name: Continental Route Contract
s.description: Two major courier companies are bidding for a contract to route a time-critical shipment across the country. Each company must choose between an Express bid, built around faster routing, and an Economy bid, built around lower-cost routing.

s.name: Quarry Blasting Windows
s.description: A small quarry's foreman chooses between an Early Window and a Late Window for a routine blast. Its haul-road coordinator chooses between Open Access and Stagger Access while arranging movement around the blast area.

s.name: Ski-Lift Grooming
s.description: A ski-lift operator and a trail-maintenance crew coordinate grooming around a shared lift. The operator chooses Early Grooming or Late Grooming for the lift's main run, while the crew chooses Dawn Grooming or Evening Grooming for the connecting trail.

s.name: Marsh Grazing Schedule
s.description: Two neighboring grazing associations hold rights to use the same salt marsh for the coming season. Each association must choose between Spring Access and Late Access for its herd.

s.name: Stadium Concession Pricing
s.description: A stadium operator and its concession partner are setting prices for food and drinks during a major championship event. Each chooses between Premium Pricing, which emphasizes higher per-item prices, and Value Pricing, which emphasizes lower listed prices.

s.name: Millpond Sluice Timing
s.description: An upstream miller and a downstream miller share a millpond and must each choose when to adjust their sluice. The upstream miller chooses Open Early or Open Late, while the downstream miller chooses Release Early or Release Late.

s.name: Seasonal Quota Contract
s.description: A regional fishing cooperative and a seafood processor are negotiating a season-long quota contract with substantial financial and reputational stakes. The cooperative chooses between Front-Loaded Catch and Steady Catch, while the processor chooses between Flexible Purchase and Firm Purchase.

s.name: Oyster Bed Leases
s.description: Two neighboring oyster growers are deciding how to handle adjacent bed leases for the coming season. Grower A chooses Lease together or Keep separate, and Grower B chooses Lease together or Keep separate.

s.name: Letterpress Run Scheduling
s.description: A small publishing house is scheduling a letterpress run for a seasonal title and chooses either Large Run or Short Run. The letterpress shop chooses either Priority Slot or Open Slot for its press schedule before the job is booked, with the decision carrying substantial budget and reputation stakes.

s.name: Migration Station Slots
s.description: A national bird observatory and a migratory-bird research consortium must coordinate access to a critical bird-ringing station during a migration window whose records will guide major conservation decisions. The observatory chooses Reserved Slot, keeping its session exclusive, or Shared Slot, dividing station time; the consortium chooses Dawn Access or Evening Access for its field session.

s.name: Satellite Downlink Windows
s.description: An Earth-observation team is choosing between an Early Window and a Late Window for its satellite downlink. A regional communications provider is choosing between a Shared Slot and a Reserved Slot for coordinating that transmission.

s.name: Shared Rail Timetable
s.description: Two freight rail operators are setting schedules for a shared corridor before the peak shipping season. Operator A chooses between Early slots and Late slots, while Operator B chooses between Hold capacity and Release capacity.

s.name: The Landmark Edition
s.description: A major publisher and a letterpress printworks are coordinating a nationally anticipated book launch with major commercial consequences for both parties. The publisher chooses between Large Run and Limited Run, while the printworks chooses between New Plates and Existing Plates.

s.name: Small Bean Restock
s.description: A small coffee roastery and a neighborhood café are coordinating a minor coffee-bean restock. The roastery chooses Local lot, buying from a nearby supplier, or Reserve lot, drawing from its regular reserve; the café chooses Morning pickup or Later pickup for collecting the beans.

s.name: Greenhouse Heat Sharing
s.description: Two neighboring commercial greenhouse operators, North Glasshouse and South Glasshouse, are coordinating one season's heat-sharing schedule. North chooses either Morning Release or Evening Release for making heat available, while South chooses either Morning Draw or Evening Draw for requesting shared heat.

s.name: Edition Run
s.description: A publisher is preparing a high-stakes letterpress edition and must choose between Full Run, printing the entire edition at once, and Staged Run, releasing it in batches. The letterpress printer must choose between Premium Stock, using specially commissioned paper, and Standard Stock, using its regular press paper.

s.name: Cave-Ripening Schedule
s.description: A farmhouse cheesemaker and a cave steward coordinate the ripening of a season’s valuable wheels. The cheesemaker chooses between Early Turn and Deep Ripen, while the steward chooses between Open Vent and Seal Cave.

s.name: Orchard Harvest Contract
s.description: A major orchard cooperative and a juice processor are setting the terms of an orchard harvest contract. The cooperative chooses Early harvest or Late harvest, while the processor chooses Spot purchase or Guaranteed contract.

s.name: Scouring Schedule
s.description: Two small wool mills serve the same local scouring queue. Each mill chooses between keeping its usual scouring capacity or making a small trim to that capacity for the day.

s.name: Lock-Keeper Shift Swap
s.description: Two neighboring canal lock-keepers are arranging an ordinary shift swap. Lock-keeper A chooses either Keep Morning or Swap Morning, while lock-keeper B chooses either Take Morning or Take Evening.

s.name: Seasonal Film Releases
s.description: Two film studios, Studio A and Studio B, are scheduling releases for high-profile films in the same season. Each chooses between an Early Release and a Late Release.

s.name: Industrial Kiln Run
s.description: A ceramics manufacturer and a specialty-clay supplier are coordinating a high-stakes production run in a shared industrial kiln. The manufacturer chooses between “Early firing” and “Late firing,” while the supplier chooses between “Rapid ramp” and “Gentle ramp” for the kiln schedule.

s.name: Shared Silage Clamp
s.description: Two neighboring dairy farmers share a small silage clamp. Farmer A chooses how firmly to compact their layer, while Farmer B chooses how quickly to load theirs.

s.name: Thatching Crew Rotas
